author: Bala Yogesh
title: 5 Technology ETFS for Investor Consideration
text:
Bala Yogesh - July 18th, 2018
Interested in investing in technology ETFs? Here the Investing News Network (INN) takes a look at the top five for investor consideration.

While the global tech market will grow by four percent to US$3 trillion in 2018, the US tech market is set to cross US$1.5 trillion mark say the reports from Forrester, making it an ample opportunity for investing in technology ETFs (exchange traded funds).
According to two separate reports by the firm, the global tech market will benefit from the improving economies with seven countries including the United States will see a growth rate of over four percent.
In the US, the firm further pointed out that the sector witnessed its fastest growth rate from 2002 [until when?] but could slow down to 5.5 percent in 2019–which would still be higher than most countries. With such a huge potential in the tech sector–at a global scale and in the US–investors might consider this as an opportunity to jump into the sector.
While there are multiple ways of investing ETFs are a popular alternative for investors. Although ETFs are bought and sold under as one stock on the exchange, they can be marketable securities that track an index, a commodity or a collection of assets.
There are at least 63 technology ETFs, including the top five listed below in the US with these funds consisting of a diverse portfolio of stocks. As such, it’s considered as a safe and easy for investors to enter into the sector as the huge holdings of these funds mitigate risks for investors.
On that note, here the Investing News Network (INN) looks at these ETFs in detail. It has to be noted that all numbers and figure are current as July 18, 2018. 1. Technology Select Sector SPDR (NYSEARCA: XLK )
Net assets:US$22.12 billion; current price: US$72.91
The first listed of our technology ETFs list is the Technology Select Sector SPDR. The net assets of this fund is one of the largest in the sector at US$22.12 billion. There are 76 holdings in this ETF, which was incepted on December 16, 1998. It has to be noted that XLK avoids most of the smaller and mid-cap companies and instead focuses on big names in this sector.
The top holdings of XLK are Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL ) weighted at 13.94 percent, Microsoft (NASDAQ: MSFT ) at 11.88 percent, Facebook (NASDAQ: FB ) at 7.37 percent. Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOGL ) weighted at 5.33 percent and Visa (NYSE: V ) with 3.71 percent are also on its list. 2. Vanguard Information Technology (NYSEARCA: VGT )
Net assets:US$21.34 billion; current price: US$190.64
Funded in January 26, 2004, Vanguard has the most diverse portfolio with focus on small and micro-caps as well as the large-cap companies.
VGT has 353 holdings but the top holdings are similar to XLK with different weightage. Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL ) weighs at 15.46 percent in this fund while Microsoft (NASDAQ: MSFT ) is second with a 12.25 percentage followed by Visa (NYSE: V ) with a 3.98 percent weighting and Intel (NASDAQ: INTC ) with a 3.88 percent weight.
